Ultraviolet Light
We are surrounded by light every day.
In fact, many different kinds of
light shape our world in ways that we do not always think about.
Not only does
light help us see, but it also makes us feel happier and helps us sleep better.
Among the many kinds of light, ultraviolet (UV) light is particularly interestin9,
as it affects our lives in manv different wavs.
UV light
is a type of radiation that comes from the sun, and
it
is divided
into three types: UVA, UVB, and UVC.
UVA makes up about 95% of the UV
radiation that reaches Earth and gives off the least amount of energy・However,
it
is potentially harmful because
it can penetrate, or reach, deep into human
skin.
UVB
is mostly blocked by the atmosphere, making up the remaining 5%
of the radiation Earth receives.
Exposure to UVB increases the risk of cellular
damage and DNA mutations
in living organisms.
UVC, on the other hand,
gives off the most energy and is the most dangerous.
However, it is completely
blocked by the Earth's atmosphere.
People only encounter UVC from special
products like sanitizing lamps.
Besides, these products are typically built with
features to Drotect us from the radiation.
One of the benefits of UV light is that it helps our bodies produce vitamin
D, which is important for our health.
Vitamin D helps the absorption of calcium,
which
is responsible
for building strong bones and muscles.
It also helps
improve heart function, reduces symptoms of depression
(a medical condition
that makes a person feel sad or hopeless), and strengthens the immune system,
which keeps us healthy. We can get a small amount of vitamin D from food, but
the best natural source of it is sunlight.
－①－26－

While UV light
is beneficial,
it can also be harmful・Too much UV light
damages
all skin types, causing early aging, wrinkles, and sometimes even
cancer
However, not all skin is affected in the same way.
For instance, lighter
skin burns quickly in the sun, while darker skin absorbs more UV light and
bums less easily.
Too much UV light can also affect our eyes, increasing the
risk of cataracts, a condition where the lens of the eye becomes cloudy.
Over
time,
it can also break down proteins in the eyes, possibly leading to loss of
sight.
The same qualities of UV light that create risks for us can also be used
to make us safer.
For example, humans can create UVC light and use
it to
kill germs, tiny harmful organisms.
Hospitals have been using this method to
clean equipment, and even the air inside of rooms for decades.
The UVC light
destroys the ability of germs to reproduce, limiting their ability to spread.
Despite the effectiveness of using UVC light to clean rooms, it is necessary
to understand some of the possible
risks.
When using UV light indoors,
chemical reactions happen.
These reactions turn the oxygen in a room into
ozone, which is a dangerous type of gas.
The ozone created can lead to more
chemical reactions that produce other dangerous chemicals.
As rooms often
have limited airnow, these harmful substances can build up.
Over time, the air
becomes dangerous to breathe.
When using UV light indoors, you must make
sure enough fresh air is provided.
UV light
is everywhere, so
it is important to understand how
it affects
us and what we can do to protect ourselves.
Although it is not realistic or
healthy to avoid UV light completely, there are ways to minimize its risks.
For
example, when spending time outdoors, you should use sunscreen, which can
help block harmful UV light.
Additionally, hats and sunglasses are also great fOr
protecting the skin and eyes.
UV rays can also penetrate clouds and still cause
harm, so these precautions should be taken no matter the weather.
Finally,
if
you are using UV light inside, remember to keep a window open to reduce the
effects of harmful gases.
UV light is both our friend and our enemy．It can bring us great health
benefits, but if we are not careful, it can also cause great harm.
－①－27－
